Excluded, decided on #1774. Reached via the Dataverse API (doi:10.7910/DVN/1KDJTZ) -- access is not the problem. The record holds a single file with 15 columns: Age, Education Level, Nationality and bare CFC1-CFC12. No codebook, no questionnaire, no wording anywhere, and the IRW dictionary row is empty (no Description, no Reference, no DOI). The only evidence tying the table to the Consideration of Future Consequences scale is the column prefix. Shipping it would mean assigning canonical CFC wording (Strathman et al. 1994) to CFC1-CFC12 by assumed publication order with nothing in the record stating that order, no author or paper to check against, and no statistical route since all 12 items share one 1-5 scale -- so a wrong ordering would be undetectable and entirely plausible, the gilbert_meta_35 failure mode. Weaker than the galindo_2023_* tables excluded earlier, which at least had a named study and a code-to-subscale map. Retryable if a paper for this dataset ever surfaces.

Blocked by batch_016 (2026-09-03). Eedi publishes no question wording as text -- NeurIPS 2020 Education Challenge guide arXiv:2007.12061 section 2.2: 'The question wording is contained in the images but will not be made available as text.' The 948 task-3/4 questions have images under data/images/, but the same paragraph bars reuse outside the competition, so OCR is not a route. Separately, this table carries two response-data defects found during extraction: item codes 1-948 each pool two different questions (the task-1/2 and task-3/4 releases are anonymised separately and the guide forbids linking their IDs, but data/neurlps_2020.R rbinds them and sets item = question_id + 1), and resp conflates IsCorrect with AnswerValue. See verify_neurips_2020.R, which reproduces both quota-free.

Blocked by batch_016 (2026-09-03). The NeurIPS 2022 Eedi starter kit (307MB, six entries) carries no question content at all -- no stems, no options, no images -- and the instruction PDF documents QuestionId purely as an identifier. Worse than the 2020 release, which at least ships images. The only route to item text is a data request to Eedi; recommend treating as permanently source-blocked rather than re-queueing. Recovered anyway and recorded in verify_neurips_2022.R: the bare-integer item code is the 1-based rank of QuestionId in ascending numeric order (0 mismatches across all 5,730 items; the rival first-appearance-order hypothesis mismatches 5,676). CorrectAnswer is present in the source for all 5,730, so correct_response is fillable the day the wording exists.

Blocked by batch_016 (2026-09-03). NOT a source problem -- the table is transposed. data/concretewords.R sets item <- x$Participant and id <- x$Expression, so the IRW item axis holds anonymous Qualtrics rater IDs and the rated multiword expressions sit in id. Confirmed from server-side aggregates: 1831/1831 item codes match ^R_[A-Za-z0-9]{15,17}$ and 0/1831 contain a space, which is impossible for a corpus of English multiword expressions. Item text is therefore unfillable by any future pass: a respondent ID has no stem. If the table were re-derived with item = Expression, item text would be trivially available because the expressions are self-describing -- that is a data change, tracked separately. Note availability_audit_full.csv classifies this AVAILABLE on the reasoning that 'the openly published norms dataset is the actual list of rated expressions', which is true of the study and false of the IRW item axis; that row should be revised.
